claims.text: A MoS2–polymer composite will exhibit enhanced self-lubricating properties at high temperatures.
A MoS2–polymer composite will exhibit enhanced mechanical strength at high temperatures.
Heat treatment can simulate the high-temperature service conditions relevant to the composite.
The interaction between MoS2 layers and the polymer matrix is the structural mediator of performance.
At elevated temperatures, MoS2 layers provide a low-friction surface.
At elevated temperatures up to 300°C, the polymer matrix maintains the composite's structural integrity.
The MoS2–polymer composite will maintain stable tribological performance across the tested temperature range up to 300°C.
The composite will have a lower friction coefficient than a standard polymer without MoS2 under the same high-temperature conditions.
The composite will maintain its mechanical strength across the tested temperature range.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome treats maintained mechanical strength as confirmation, whereas the falsification rule states that maintaining mechanical strength compared with the baseline would falsify the hypothesis. The rule likely intended failure to maintain strength.
